terms.definition: Run gen_atomic_mass.py --check: regenerate AtomicMass.lean from the data table and diff it against the committed file. Any divergence exits 1 with a unified diff and fails the PR — a Lean file that compiles must not carry numbers the table no longer produces.
An independent adversarial reviewer builds the strongest mathematical and formal case that the statement, proof or model framing is false, vacuous, over-claimed or missing a hypothesis.

An independent reviewer reads only the `.lean` declaration and proof and states in mathematical prose what hypotheses, quantifiers, objects and conclusion it proves, without seeing the block's `.md` narrative.
A second independent reviewer reads only the `.md` narrative statement and proof and writes the formal hypotheses, quantifiers, objects and conclusion it claims, without seeing the `.lean` file.

Write the narrative statement and narrative proof in the block's `.md` and the formal statement and proof in its `.lean`. Write the Lean statement first and ask whether it could be false. An unproved step is `sorry` with a citation; a dependence on a conjecture is an explicit class hypothesis. A number in prose is read from its witness.

Same hypotheses, same quantifier order, same conclusion, same objects, in both directions. The narrative proof's logical skeleton is compared with the Lean proof's in the same way. A difference either way is a finding.
Compile against the real import cone; record `#print axioms` and `sorry` status for the new declarations.

Schema validation, reference and citation resolution, math render, vacuity audit (no `True` conclusions, no empty conjecture classes, no uncited `sorry`), and witness staleness for every quoted number.
The author inspects the block triple, its mechanical verdicts and the independent equivalence and adversarial review records on the pull request, and merges the change set.

Search the folio's blocks, its compute and its ingested library (section text and extracted candidates of every held source) before drafting. A result settled in a held paper is cited, not re-derived.
Demote the block to a conjecture, or state the open step with `sorry` and a citation, and record the gap in the work plan. Never weaken the statement until it passes.
The author names the claim, the objects it is about, and the sources it rests on, before any text is drafted.

terms.prefLabel: Build the doc-gen4 render over the warm cache
terms.definition: Tool `lean-html-docs` (`adapters/paper/lean/lean-docs-build.sh --lake-root <pkg> --lib <Lib>`). Reads the SOURCE, the folio's Lake packages. Refuses while another lake/lean process holds `.lake/`, refuses over a restored tree with no traces, checks or restores the warm cache, enables the sentinel-commented doc-gen4 require for this build only, then `lake -R -Kenv=dev build <Lib>:docs`. Output: `<pkg>/.lake/build/doc-data` (the per-module declaration data the viewer is made from) and `<pkg>/.lake/build/doc` (the static HTML, kept only as the fallback): working directories, not yet anything a site reads.

`bun run cat state:mount` (or `branch-store.ts mount --id <id>`) at the start of the site build, as for `beans/`: puts the branch tip on disk at the declared path. Reads the RENDER; writes nothing to the branch. A site build of a folio whose Lean did not change starts here.

terms.prefLabel: Publish the render at its route, railed
terms.definition: A site step of the folio's declared build (`site.build.siteSteps`). Reads the mounted RENDER, writes the PUBLISHED pages at `<site>/<route>/`, the route the declaration's `coverage.visualiser` names: the KG viewer and its `data/` shards are copied as they are, and the site build's own rail pass (`rail-standalone-pages.ts --foreign-site`, which runs after every site step) puts the harness rail on the viewer page, so the rail's assets are the site's and nothing extra lands at its root. Fallback, when the store holds doc-gen4's static HTML instead: Tool `lean-render-publish` (`adapters/paper/lean/lean-render.ts --docs <mount path> --site <site> --route <route> --no-rail`) stages it without Lake's bookkeeping, marks its iframe navbar and `find/` redirect rail-declined and adds the layout shim. The document site's ∀ panel links each declaration to the viewer opened at it, `<route>/#/m/<Module>/<name>`.

terms.prefLabel: Write the KG render to the Lean branch store
terms.definition: Tool `lean-kg-publish` (`adapters/paper/lean/lean-kg-publish.ts --doc-data <pkg>/.lake/build/doc-data --site <checkout> --route <store path> --no-rail`) writes the viewer page and its `data/` shards into the mounted store's path (the folio's declared `lean` graph, e.g. `lean/`), then `bun folio-assistant/cat-harness-tools/scripts/branch-store.ts push --id <id>`. The store is tip-keyed: the branch tip IS the current render, with a root `manifest.json` (`state-manifest/v1`); the push splices onto the tip and never forces. The render is never committed to the folio's main.

Process_BeanClose: end the bean in a state that says why — complete and archive it, scrap it with its reasons and archive it, or record the blocker and hand it back. The one place resolve and archive are drawn (bean m8gz, owner 2026-10-24); placed straight before the end so the engine's resolve sees nothing left but the archive step.

Process_BeanOpen: check before you create, find out whose the bean is, and claim it — or leave it alone when it is someone else's. The one place a claim is drawn (bean m8gz, owner 2026-10-24); the gateway after this reads which end it reached.

Core's shared review-and-publish process (Process_FolioReviewPublish): the reviewer reads the rendered folio and approves it, asks for changes, or sends a working draft to the Authoring Committee. Before 2026-11-01 each authoring process drew these steps itself (shared block G6, owner Q-BR-7 A).
Every block edit runs the HCI validation gate — see editing-hci-validation.bpmn.

Give each formal block (definition, theorem, lemma, proposition, corollary, conjecture, proof) a .lean sibling that Lean 4 accepts, in the order lean-formalization sets out. A compiling declaration is not a formalised claim: check vacuity and narrative drift before calling it done, and record the status with proof-verification.
Scope the paper: chapters, the blocks each needs, what gets formalised.

Typeset the paper through LaTeX to PDF and HTML. Run latex_preflight first — missing packages, fonts or engine — rather than discovering them twenty minutes in. The preamble, class and macros belong to the folio, never to the platform.

Create the folio repository with `bun run cat init-folio` (or the folio_init tool): content/, the document, chapter and first block manifests, the builder shim, AGENTS.md, .mcp.json, the session-start hook and the beans store, with the platform linked rather than copied.
The plan becomes beans, so a resumed session or a sibling agent can pick it up.
Run content validation over the folio: schemas, the content profile (formal kinds only in a paper), cross-block consistency and that the Lean builds. Loop back rather than rendering over a failure.
